title: Design a Visual / Embedding-Based Image Search System
prompt: Design a visual search system: given a query image (or text), return visually similar images from a very large catalog. It must embed content, index embeddings for approximate nearest-neighbor retrieval, and rank results, all at low latency and high recall. Assume billions of images and continuous ingestion.
blurb: Embedding-based retrieval at billion scale: encoders, ANN indexes, reranking, and keeping embeddings/index fresh as the catalog and model change.

rubric.label: Requirements gathering
rubric.description: Separates functional (embed, index, k-NN retrieve, rerank, filter, multimodal query) from non-functional (p99 latency, recall@k, index freshness, availability, cost).

rubric.label: Clarifying questions
rubric.description: Asks about catalog size, query volume, latency budget, recall vs precision needs, query modality (image/text/both), metadata filtering, freshness.

rubric.label: Back-of-envelope estimations
rubric.description: Derives embedding dimension × count → index memory, QPS, per-query ANN + rerank cost, embedding compute/GPU for ingestion, storage.

rubric.label: Embedding model & pipeline
rubric.description: Encoder choice (CNN/ViT/CLIP-style), shared image/text space for multimodal query, batch embedding of catalog, normalization, embedding versioning.

rubric.label: ANN index design
rubric.description: HNSW/IVF-PQ tradeoffs, recall vs latency vs memory, quantization/compression, sharding billions of vectors, distributed search + merge.

rubric.label: Retrieval + reranking
rubric.description: ANN candidate retrieval → precise rerank (exact distance / cross-encoder / metadata + business rules), metadata filtering (pre vs post), diversity.

rubric.label: Embedding consistency & skew
rubric.description: Same encoder + preprocessing for query and index, handling embedding-model version changes (must re-embed everything), avoiding mixed-version index.

rubric.label: Evaluation & drift
rubric.description: Recall@k / precision@k / mAP against labeled sets, online engagement metrics, monitoring retrieval quality and catalog/embedding drift over time.

rubric.label: High-level design
rubric.description: Ingest → embed → index build/update; query → embed → ANN retrieve → rerank → filter → results; async re-embedding on model change.

rubric.label: Scaling & reliability
rubric.description: Sharded/replicated vector index, scatter-gather, incremental index updates vs periodic rebuild, caching, graceful degradation, GPU fleet for embedding.

rubric.label: Observability
rubric.description: Latency per stage, recall/quality metrics, index freshness/lag, embedding version tracking, cache hit rate, drift alerts.

rubric.label: Safety, abuse & privacy
rubric.description: Filtering unsafe/illegal images, copyright/dedup, query privacy, preventing scraping, face/biometric considerations.

functional_requirements: Embed query (image or text) and catalog images into a shared vector space
Retrieve k approximate nearest neighbors from a billion-scale index
Rerank candidates for precision (exact distance / cross-encoder / business rules)
Filter by metadata (category, availability, safe-content) and diversify
Continuously ingest and index new/updated images
nonfunctional_requirements: High recall@k with acceptable precision after rerank
Fresh index — new images searchable within minutes
Cost-efficient memory for billions of vectors
clarifying_questions: Query by image, by text, or both (multimodal)?
Recall vs precision priority, and k?
Do we filter by metadata, and how selective are filters?
How fresh must newly-added images be?
qualifying_questions: Is exact-duplicate detection a separate need from similarity search?
Are there hard metadata filters that must be applied pre-retrieval?
How often does the embedding model change (forcing full re-embedding)?

estimations.index_memory: 2B images × 512-dim float32 = ~4TB raw; PQ/quantization compresses ~8-32x → hundreds of GB, sharded across nodes
estimations.traffic: ~20K QPS; each query = 1 embedding + ANN search over shards + rerank of top candidates
estimations.query_cost: Query embed ~5-20ms GPU; ANN search ~5-20ms/shard scatter-gather; rerank top-few-hundred exact/cross-encoder
estimations.ingestion: Continuous new images → GPU embedding fleet; incremental index insert + periodic rebuild
estimations.storage: Raw images in blob store; embeddings + metadata in vector index + KV; petabyte-scale blob

data_model: images(image_id PK, blob_uri, metadata, embedding_version, indexed_at)
vectors(image_id, embedding[], shard) in ANN index
api_design: POST /v1/search { image|text, k, filters{} } → [{image_id, score, ...}], query_id
POST /internal/index/upsert { image_id, embedding, metadata } → incremental insert
POST /internal/reembed { embedding_version } → triggers catalog re-embedding + reindex
reference.high_level_design: Ingestion pushes new images to a GPU embedding service that produces vectors with an explicit embedding-model version; vectors and metadata are inserted into a sharded ANN index (incremental inserts plus periodic full rebuilds for optimal graph/quantization). At query time, the query (image or text) is embedded with the same encoder/preprocessing into the shared space, ANN search scatter-gathers across shards to retrieve a candidate set with high recall, then a reranker computes exact distances (or a cross-encoder) and applies metadata filters and business/diversity rules to produce final results. Metadata filtering is done pre- or post-retrieval depending on selectivity. Query embeddings and hot results are cached. When the embedding model changes, the whole catalog must be re-embedded and reindexed under the new version — never mixing versions in one index. Quality is monitored with recall@k/precision@k offline and engagement online, plus index-freshness and drift monitoring.

deep_dives.probe: Choose an ANN index for billions of vectors. Walk me through HNSW vs IVF-PQ — recall, latency, memory, and build/update cost — and how quantization changes the tradeoff.
The index doesn't fit on one node. How do you shard billions of vectors and do distributed search — scatter-gather, per-shard top-k, merge — and what about hot shards and partial results?
ANN gives approximate candidates. Why rerank, and with what — exact distances, a heavier cross-encoder, metadata/business rules? How many candidates do you rerank to fit latency?
You improve the encoder. Now query and index embeddings are in different spaces. How do you re-embed billions of images and cut over without serving mixed-version, incompatible vectors?
Users filter by category/availability. Do you filter before or after ANN retrieval? What breaks if a highly selective filter is applied post-retrieval?
How do you measure that retrieval is good — recall@k/precision@k against labeled pairs offline, and what online signal — and how do you catch quality regressions after a reindex?
An image's content or metadata is updated, or new images arrive continuously. How does the index stay in sync — change-stream driving re-embed + upsert — and what's the lag before it's searchable?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions index or embedding or vector
followup_bank.question: When a source image or its metadata changes (or new ones are added), how does the ANN index stay in sync — CDC/change-stream driving re-embedding and upsert vs periodic rebuild? What's the freshness lag before it's searchable?

You cache query embeddings / hot results. What's the eviction policy, and when the embedding model version or an image changes, how do you invalidate stale-after-change cached embeddings so you don't return results from an old space?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions ANN or HNSW or IVF or quantization
followup_bank.question: How does your chosen index trade recall vs latency vs memory, and how do you tune it (efSearch/nprobe) per query budget?
How many candidates do you rerank and with what, to fit the latency budget while recovering precision the ANN stage lost?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions model or encoder or version
followup_bank.question: When you upgrade the encoder, how do you re-embed the whole catalog and cut over without a mixed-version index?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions recall or precision or evaluation
followup_bank.question: How do you measure retrieval quality offline (recall@k against labeled sets) and catch a regression after a reindex?

scaling: Shard vectors across nodes; scatter-gather top-k with merge
Replicate shards for QPS + availability; partial results on shard timeout
Quantization (PQ/OPQ) to fit billions of vectors in memory
Incremental inserts + periodic full rebuild for index quality
GPU embedding fleet autoscaled for ingestion bursts; cache query embeddings
bottlenecks: Index memory footprint at billion scale
Re-embedding the whole catalog on model change
tradeoffs: Recall vs latency vs memory in ANN tuning
Incremental updates (fresh) vs periodic rebuild (optimal index)
Pre-filter (correct, index-complex) vs post-filter (simple, recall loss)
alternative_solutions: Exact k-NN (only viable for small catalogs)
LSH-based ANN (simpler, weaker recall/latency than graph/IVF)
Perceptual-hash matching for exact/near-duplicate detection alongside semantic search
observability: Recall@k / precision@k on labeled sets + online CTR/engagement
Drift alerts on retrieval quality after reindex/model change
security: Filter unsafe/illegal images from results (safe-content flags)
Query image privacy; avoid storing sensitive queries
Anti-scraping + rate limiting on the search API
reference.reference_answer: A strong answer embeds query and catalog into a shared space with the same encoder/preprocessing, then builds a sharded ANN index (HNSW or IVF-PQ) tuned for recall-vs-latency-vs-memory with quantization to fit billions of vectors, doing distributed scatter-gather search. It follows retrieval with a reranking stage — exact distances or a cross-encoder plus metadata/business filters — recovering the precision the approximate stage traded away, and reasons about pre- vs post-filtering by selectivity. It treats the embedding model version as first-class: an encoder upgrade requires re-embedding the entire catalog and a clean cutover, never mixing incompatible vectors in one index. It keeps the index fresh via a change-driven re-embed/upsert pipeline, caches query embeddings and hot results with version-aware invalidation, and evaluates with recall@k/precision@k offline plus online engagement, monitoring for quality drift after every reindex or model change.

interviewer_notes: The backbone here is the retrieve-then-rerank pattern over a sharded ANN index; make sure the candidate reaches it rather than proposing exact k-NN over billions of vectors. Push concretely on ANN choice (HNSW vs IVF-PQ) and the recall/latency/memory triangle including quantization — a senior candidate can tune efSearch/nprobe against a latency budget and explain sharding + scatter-gather. Two senior separators: (1) embedding versioning and consistency — an encoder change puts query and index in different spaces, forcing a full re-embed and clean cutover; a candidate who ignores this has a subtle correctness bug; and (2) evaluation — recall@k/precision@k against labeled sets and catching regressions after a reindex (the ml-specifics/eval dimension). When they mention the index/embeddings, hit the CDC/freshness probe: how new/changed images get re-embedded and become searchable, and the lag. When they add an embedding or result cache, probe eviction and, importantly, stale-after-change invalidation when the model version or an image changes. Also probe pre- vs post-metadata-filtering (post-filtering a selective filter silently destroys recall). Reserve time for drift monitoring and the re-embedding cutover. Weak candidates stop at 'compute embeddings and do nearest neighbor'; strong ones design a sharded, versioned, reranked, freshness-managed retrieval system.
